- **FPS:** a counter on screen shows the current frame rate.

{"path":"effect_gouraud_shaded_cube_anthropic-claude-opus-5-5_01.html","edit_description":"Create a single self-contained HTML file (no external libs, Canvas 2D only, no WebGL). Full-window dark canvas. Rendering: use an offscreen ImageData framebuffer at a reduced resolution (e.g. 480x360-ish scaled to fit, keeping aspect) drawn to the visible canvas with putImageData then drawImage scaled with imageSmoothingEnabled=false, or render directly at canvas size with ImageData (Uint32Array view) — choose internal buffer ~ 640x480 scaled up.
Pipeline:
- Cube 8 vertices (±1), 6 faces each with 4 vertex indices in CCW order when viewed from outside, split into 2 triangles each (12 triangles).
- Per-vertex normals: averaged normals (vertex position normalized) for smooth Gouraud look; each face has a base color (distinct colors per face) — per-vertex lighting computed per face-vertex so color = faceColor * (ambient 0.15 + diffuse Lambert max(0, N·L)) plus a small light color tint; also optional specular-free.
- Rotation matrices: build 3x3 rotX, rotY, rotZ matrices and multiply; angles advance by dt.
- Moving light source: point light orbiting the cube (position animated with sin/cos over time); L = normalize(lightPos - vertexWorldPos). Draw the light as a small glowing dot projected on screen (drawn on top after the framebuffer, using 2D arc with radial gradient) if in front of camera.
- Camera at z = -4 (or translate cube to z=+4), perspective projection: x' = x*f/z + cx, y' = -y*f/z + cy, f based on buffer height.
- Backface culling: compute screen-space signed area of the projected triangle; skip if facing away (choose sign consistent with winding; verify: cube vertices order front face so it's correct). Also alternatively compute using view-space normal dot view vector; use screen-space 2D cross product.
- Rasterizer: scanline or bounding-box barycentric with edge functions and top-left fill rule, interpolating r,g,b across the triangle; z-buffer (Float32Array) with interpolated 1/z for correctness (not strictly needed with culling on convex cube, but include). Write pixels to Uint32Array (ABGR little endian). Clear buffer each frame with a subtle vertical gradient background (precompute background array and copy with set()).
- Wireframe toggle W: when on, draw triangle edges (visible triangles only, including the diagonal) with ctx lines on the visible canvas over (or instead of) the shaded mode — make it: wireframe mode shows lines only in color of per-vertex lit colors? Simply: wireframe mode draws lines instead of filled rasterization, lines colored bright cyan; plus vertex dots.
- Pause P: freezes rotation and light motion (time accumulation stops) but keeps rendering and FPS counting.
- FPS display: HUD top-left text updated every 0.5s showing FPS, mode (Shaded/Wireframe), paused state, triangle count drawn, and help "W: wireframe  P: pause". Use monospace font.
- requestAnimationFrame loop, dt clamped to 0.1s. Handle resize.
Make sure winding is correct: define faces with vertex indices such that (v1-v0)x(v2-v0) points outward, and with projection y flipped, visible triangles have a consistent sign; compute cull using the view-space: normal = cross(b-a, c-a) in camera space, visible if dot(normal, a - camera) < 0. Use this 3D test for robustness (camera at origin, cube translated to z=4, looking +z). Note with camera looking +z and y flipped in projection, handle rasterizer to accept either winding (use absolute area / flip edges when area negative) so culling alone decides visibility."}
